incidents.vector: Voice phishing / social engineering against employees and exploitation of Free-For-Teacher accounts to access cloud infrastructure.
incidents.impact: ShinyHunters claimed a second successive breach after a May 1 disclosure, defacing the Canvas login page with a ransom demand and forcing Instructure to take the platform offline mid-finals; group says it stole 3.65TB including names, emails, student IDs and billions of private messages from K-12 districts and universities including Princeton, Columbia, Stanford, UPenn, Manchester (UK) and Universidad del Desarrollo (Chile), with deadline pushed to May 12.

incidents.vector: Active exploitation of zero-day CVE-2026-6973, an improper input validation flaw allowing authenticated administrators to execute code remotely on EPMM servers.
incidents.impact: Ivanti disclosed limited in-the-wild exploitation alongside four additional high-severity flaws; CISA added the bug to its KEV catalog within hours. The defect appears linked to fallout from January's CVE-2026-1281/-1340 mass exploitation that hit nearly 100 victims including Dutch government bodies, with admin credentials likely harvested during that campaign now being reused.

incidents.vector: Microsoft Teams social engineering — external chat invites lured employees into screen-sharing sessions where attackers harvested VPN credentials and deployed remote management tooling.
incidents.impact: Rapid7 attributed an apparent Chaos ransomware extortion attempt to Iran's MuddyWater group, which is using ransomware branding as a false-flag cover for state espionage and data theft; data was stolen and published, but no encryption was deployed, consistent with MOIS prepositioning across Western and Middle Eastern networks.

incidents.victim: Polish water utilities (Jabłonna Lacka, Szczytno, Małdyty, Tolkmicko, Sierakowo)
incidents.vector: Compromise of administrator accounts on industrial control systems exposed at five small-town water treatment plants.
incidents.impact: Poland's ABW intelligence service publicly disclosed that attackers reached ICS in some facilities and altered pump and alarm settings, creating a direct risk to water supply continuity; CyberDefence24 had previously linked the campaign to a pro-Russian hacktivist group, and ABW framed the attacks as part of a broader Russian destabilization effort against NATO/EU states.

incidents.victim: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS firewall customers
incidents.vector: Exploitation of zero-day CVE-2026-0300, a buffer overflow in the User-ID Captive Portal allowing unauthenticated remote code execution as root via crafted packets.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 is tracking activity cluster CL-STA-1132 exploiting the flaw against internet-exposed firewalls; attackers injected shellcode into nginx, deployed open-source EarthWorm and ReverseSocks5 tunneling tools, conducted Active Directory enumeration, executed a SAML flood to pivot to a second device, and methodically destroyed forensic logs.

incidents.victim: Mexican federal and state government (tax authority, electoral institute, Mexico City civil registry, Monterrey water utility)
incidents.vector: Heavy use of an LLM coding assistant to generate exploitation tooling and orchestrate attacks against at least nine government entities, with stolen credentials reused across systems.
incidents.impact: Dragos and Gambit Security documented what they describe as the first widely successful AI-orchestrated campaign (Dec 2025 – Feb 2026), exfiltrating millions of tax and property records; attackers reached an OT gateway at Monterrey's water utility but were stopped by a login portal that resisted automated password spraying, demonstrating fundamental controls still blunt AI-assisted attacks.

incidents.victim: Government agencies in South America and southeastern Europe
incidents.vector: Initial access likely via zero-day or n-day exploits on edge appliances, followed by deployment of custom malware (NetDraft, CloudSorcerer v3, VShell/SNOWLIGHT, SNOWRUST) and reconnaissance tooling such as Impacket and gogo.
incidents.impact: Cisco Talos disclosed UAT-8302, a China-nexus APT operating against government entities in South America since late 2024 and in southeastern Europe through 2025; the group's tooling overlaps with multiple previously identified Chinese clusters and emphasizes long-term access for credential and AD intelligence collection.

incidents.vector: Compromised npm packages with a malicious preinstall hook (setup.mjs) that executed an obfuscated Bun-based credential stealer (execution.js) on install.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 attributes the "Mini Shai-Hulud" wave to the same actor behind April's @bitwarden/cli compromise; affected packages totalled ~570K weekly downloads and the payload harvested GitHub PATs, npm tokens, AWS/Azure/GCP secrets, Kubernetes tokens and Claude/MCP configs from CI runners, then propagated via a GitHub commit-search dead-drop.

incidents.victim: U.S. Department of Defense (military training data, service member records)
incidents.vector: Unauthenticated API exposed by Schemata, an AI virtual training platform contracted to DOD, leaked records over the open internet.
incidents.impact: Strix researchers reported the leak of US service member records and sensitive military course material; Schemata reportedly took roughly 150 days to secure the API after notification, raising questions about contractor vetting and incident response on defense work.

incidents.victim: Unnamed federal IT contractor serving 45+ U.S. agencies (incl. EEOC)
incidents.vector: Two recently-fired employees (twin brothers) reused privileged access to write-protect, delete and destroy 96 government databases, and trafficked a complainant's email password.
incidents.impact: A federal jury convicted Sohaib Akhter on conspiracy, password trafficking and firearms charges; the destruction targeted databases supporting federal customers including EEOC, with sentencing scheduled for September and a maximum 21-year exposure.

incidents.victim: Russian organizations in manufacturing, telecom, oil and gas
incidents.vector: Targeted phishing emails delivering BrockenDoor, Remcos and DarkGate; coordination with Head Mare for initial access and PhantomDL/PhantomCore custom malware.
incidents.impact: Kaspersky reported overlapping infrastructure between BO Team (Black Owl) and Head Mare in Q1 2026 attacks on roughly 20 Russian organizations, indicating operational coordination among pro-Ukraine groups; activity has shifted from destructive operations toward longer-term cyber espionage.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to Braintrust's AWS infrastructure, including its API key database.
incidents.impact: Braintrust disclosed a security incident and instructed customers — which include Cloudflare, Vercel and Stripe — to rotate API keys; the breadth of downstream exposure depends on how the harvested keys were used and whether AI model traffic or telemetry was accessed.

incidents.vector: Compromise of the official AVB Disc Soft distribution site for nearly a month, with attackers embedding hidden backdoors into the software installers.
incidents.impact: AVB Disc Soft has released clean versions and disclosed the supply-chain compromise; users who downloaded DAEMON Tools during the affected window may have a backdoor on their systems and need to remediate.

incidents.vector: Exploit of the Ekubo smart-contract protocol (specific flaw not disclosed in available reporting).
incidents.impact: Hackers drained roughly $1.4M in crypto assets from the Ekubo Protocol; the loss is moderate by DeFi-heist standards but underscores ongoing smart-contract risk.
